prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick one specific lawyer for you, but I can help you choose the right one and take the next steps. Here’s a practical plan to find and hire a good personal-injury lawyer in/near Pleasanton, CA.

Immediate legal/time-sensitive notes
- California personal-injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the injury. Claims against government entities usually have a much shorter deadline (often about 6 months). Don’t delay contacting counsel.
- If you haven’t already: get medical care, preserve evidence (photos, damaged vehicle, clothing), get witness contact info, and avoid giving recorded statements to insurers before talking to a lawyer.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for these essentials:
- Specialization: focuses on personal injury (car accidents, pedestrian, motorcycle, etc.), not a general practice.
- Local experience: familiar with Alameda County/Contra Costa County courts, local judges, and local insurance adjusters.
- Track record: history of settlements and verdicts for cases like yours.
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but you want a lawyer willing and able to take it to trial if necessary.
- Fee structure: contingency fee (no recovery, no fee) is common. Understand the percentage and who pays costs up front.
- Communication: clear point of contact, timely responses, and updates.
- Resources: access to accident reconstruction, medical experts, and investigators if your case needs them.
- Good standing: clean record with the California State Bar.

Where to find candidates
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service.
- California State Bar “Find a Lawyer” and attorney discipline lookup.
- Reviews on Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google/Yelp (read details, not just stars).
- Referrals from friends/family or medical providers.

Questions to ask at the first consultation
- How long have you handled auto/personal-injury cases?
- Have you handled cases like mine? What was the outcome?
- Do you handle cases on a contingency fee? What percentage do you charge? Any other fees or costs I might owe?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? Will I meet the attorney or a staff member handle most communication?
- What is your trial experience and litigation rate (how often do you go to trial)?
- What is your estimate of the case value and timeline?
- How do you communicate updates and how often?
- Can you provide references from former clients?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount or “we always win.”
- Pressuring you to sign immediately without reviewing evidence.
- Poor communication or lack of a clear fee agreement in writing.
- No track record or unwillingness to go to trial if needed.

What to bring to consultations
- Police report, photos/video of the accident and injuries, medical records/bills, insurance information, correspondence with insurers, witness contact info, repair estimates, and a written timeline of events.

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft a short script/email to contact attorneys.
- Provide a checklist to bring to consultations.
- Compile a shortlist of personal-injury attorneys that serve Pleasanton if you give me permission to search (note: I can’t browse the web from this chat, but I can guide you how to search or provide sample queries).

Do you want a phone/email script or a short list of local firms (and are you okay if I recommend how to search for up-to-date contact info)? Also, tell me a bit about the accident and injuries (severity, fault questions, any police report) and I’ll tailor the advice.
